name: GEF Small Grants Programme South Africa
summary: South Africa's SGP country programme funds community-based and civil society organisations through calls for proposals, with OP8 work centred on wildlife economy landscapes and community-led protection of threatened species.
reporting: Grantees submit progress reports to the National Coordinator with a financial report showing evidence of costs, following the programme's reporting templates, and a completion or final report.

steps: Proposal evaluation by the National Steering Committee
Ex-ante validation visit, if conditionally approved and risk-selected

eligibility.rule: Not a private company or individual entrepreneur

geography.quote: In South Africa, GEF SGP started in 2001 and since then it has supported 160 projects

access.quote: Thus, calls for proposals will encourage women-led organisations or those that have active participation of women as well as youth to submit their applications.

reporting.quote: Grantees should submit progress reports to the NC along with a financial report indicating evidence of costs for approval.

effort.quote: During proposal development, SGP applicants will be required to select relevant project level indicators aligned with GEF 8 core indicators to be provided in the application template.
Workshops also include discussions on additional or supporting documentation that may be required to aid in the evaluation of submissions by the NSC.

The SGP team would undertake ex-ante / validation visits on a risk basis to grantrequesting organisations upon conditional grant approval by the SGP National Steering Committee (NSC) and prior to the signature of the Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) between the GEF SGP and the grantee.

eligibility.quote: SGP cannot provide grant funding to private companies or individual entrepreneurs.

after_award.quote: To track implementation, grantees are expected to report progress in their achievement in their mid-term and final progress reports.

Every project should be visited at least twice in its lifetime, upon receipt of the first progress report from beneficiary organisations and during the following year or prior to completion/ final payment.
